note: Provenance for every asset wired into the bundle. An asset is wired only after its bytes are compared against the canonical source; the marks are used AS SUPPLIED, so a later edit to one of these files is a brand violation rather than a style choice. scripts/design-system/ds-audit.mjs recomputes each sha256 and fails on drift, which is what makes a silent recolor impossible to land. `mirrors` are copies of the same canonical bytes served from elsewhere in the repo; they are hashed against the same value, because a mark that is correct in the bundle and recolored in public/ is the exact failure this file exists to catch.

hazards.note: npm run gen-icons writes SOLID #005bff squares over public/pwa-192x192.png, public/pwa-512x512.png and public/apple-touch-icon.png. The icons currently on disk are mark artwork in #FFE629 and were NOT produced by this script. Running it would destroy three correct mark-derived icons and replace them with flat blue. Left alone here: this pass is an asset swap, and rewriting or removing the script is a separate call.

The APP's --gold token is #D4AF37, not the published Techmen Gold #FFE629, and --hr-regular / --hr-build carry it too. After this swap the mark on the splash, the access gate and the landing page renders canonical gold next to app chrome in the older gold; the difference is visible on the landing page, where the mark and the SIGN IN button no longer match. Left alone deliberately: changing it restyles every app surface, which is outside an asset swap.
